infrastructure: Belarus has decent urban internet connectivity inherited from Soviet-era infrastructure, though modernisation has slowed.
The Minsk data centre sector was growing pre-2020 but has stagnated due to political crisis.
IT infrastructure in Hi-Tech Park Minsk was internationally competitive, but exodus of tech companies has diminished it.
talent: Belarusian State University and BSUIR produced strong technical graduates, but most talented engineers emigrated post-2020.
Hi-Tech Park Minsk was a successful model for IT development before the political crisis.
Estimated 100,000+ tech workers have left Belarus since 2020, severely depleting the talent pool.
governance: The Lukashenko regime's authoritarian rule creates a deeply hostile environment for independent AI development.
Internet censorship, surveillance, and political repression of tech workers have driven mass emigration.
No independent AI governance exists; state AI is focused on surveillance and political control.
investment: Western sanctions imposed after the 2020 political crisis have largely cut Belarus off from international investment.
Russian state investment partially replaces Western capital, but with different priorities.
Hi-Tech Park incentives still nominally exist but have lost most international participants.
economic_readiness: The economy is deeply integrated with Russia and increasingly isolated from Western markets and technologies.
AI adoption in state enterprises is limited; private sector AI development has largely relocated to Poland, Lithuania, and Ukraine.
Economic sanctions and political instability severely constrain normal AI commercialisation pathways.
